notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Reject invalid input by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors, using the established codes: "invalid_state" for wrong invoice status, "invalid_quantity" for bad quantities, "negative_amount" for negative money. Match the message style f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}" used in issue_invoice and payments.authorize.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Normalize money with round_money before validating: Always pass incoming monetary values through ledgerly.money.round_money (and compare against ZERO) before storing them on models; never store raw floats or unrounded Decimals. round_money also raises BillingError("float_amount") for NaN/invalid input.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0003] Reject bools when validating integer fields: When validating an int parameter, exclude bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) before the isinstance(x, int) check, since True/False are ints in Python and would otherwise pass quantity validation.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

item.title: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc
item.content: In ledgerly, normalize any incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
